<script>
(function () {

  /**
   * ========================================================
   * REQUEST DETAILS VALIDATION
   *
   * Supports both:
   *
   * 1. Standard Request Details form
   *    - sf_Topic__c
   *    - sf_Sub_Topic__c
   *
   * 2. Multiple Subtopics form
   *    - sf_Sub_Topic__c only
   * ========================================================
   */

  function getRequestFields() {
    return {
      topic: document.getElementById('sf_Topic__c'),
      subtopic: document.getElementById('sf_Sub_Topic__c')
    };
  }


  /**
   * Determine whether the current node contains
   * one of our forms.
   */
  function hasRequestForm() {
    var fields = getRequestFields();

    return !!fields.subtopic;
  }


  /**
   * Validate whichever fields exist on the node.
   */
  function requestDetailsAreValid() {
    var fields = getRequestFields();

    /*
     * No relevant form on this node.
     */
    if (!fields.subtopic) {
      return true;
    }

    var subtopicValue =
      String(fields.subtopic.value || '').trim();

    /*
     * Multiple Subtopics form:
     * only Subtopic exists.
     */
    if (!fields.topic) {
      return subtopicValue !== '';
    }

    /*
     * Standard Request Details form:
     * Topic + Subtopic both exist.
     */
    var topicValue =
      String(fields.topic.value || '').trim();

    return (
      topicValue !== '' &&
      subtopicValue !== ''
    );
  }


  /**
   * Create the validation message.
   */
  function ensureValidationMessage() {
    var fields = getRequestFields();

    if (!fields.subtopic) {
      return null;
    }

    /*
     * Standard Request Details form has a grid.
     */
    var container =
      document.querySelector('.zt-form-grid');

    /*
     * Multiple Subtopics form does not use the grid,
     * so use the Subtopic field wrapper instead.
     */
    if (!container) {
      container =
        fields.subtopic.closest('.zt-form-field');
    }

    if (!container) {
      return null;
    }

    var existing =
      container.querySelector(
        '.zt-request-validation-error'
      );

    if (existing) {
      return existing;
    }

    var error =
      document.createElement('div');

    error.className =
      'zt-request-validation-error';

    error.setAttribute(
      'role',
      'alert'
    );

    error.setAttribute(
      'aria-live',
      'polite'
    );

    /*
     * Different message depending on form type.
     */
    if (fields.topic) {
      error.textContent =
        'Please select both Topic and Subtopic before continuing.';
    } else {
      error.textContent =
        'Please select a Subtopic before continuing.';
    }

    container.appendChild(error);

    return error;
  }


  /**
   * Show validation errors.
   */
  function showValidationErrors() {
    var fields = getRequestFields();

    if (!fields.subtopic) {
      return;
    }

    var error =
      ensureValidationMessage();

    var subtopicMissing =
      String(
        fields.subtopic.value || ''
      ).trim() === '';

    /*
     * Topic only needs validation if it exists.
     */
    var topicMissing = false;

    if (fields.topic) {
      topicMissing =
        String(
          fields.topic.value || ''
        ).trim() === '';
    }


    if (fields.topic) {
      fields.topic.classList.toggle(
        'zt-required-invalid',
        topicMissing
      );

      fields.topic.setAttribute(
        'aria-invalid',
        topicMissing
          ? 'true'
          : 'false'
      );
    }


    fields.subtopic.classList.toggle(
      'zt-required-invalid',
      subtopicMissing
    );

    fields.subtopic.setAttribute(
      'aria-invalid',
      subtopicMissing
        ? 'true'
        : 'false'
    );


    if (error) {
      error.classList.toggle(
        'is-visible',
        topicMissing || subtopicMissing
      );
    }


    /*
     * Focus first missing field.
     */
    if (
      fields.topic &&
      topicMissing
    ) {
      fields.topic.focus();
    } else if (subtopicMissing) {
      fields.subtopic.focus();
    }
  }


  /**
   * Refresh validation after the user changes
   * one of the dropdowns.
   */
  function refreshValidationState() {
    var fields = getRequestFields();

    if (!fields.subtopic) {
      return;
    }

    var subtopicMissing =
      String(
        fields.subtopic.value || ''
      ).trim() === '';

    var topicMissing = false;

    if (fields.topic) {
      topicMissing =
        String(
          fields.topic.value || ''
        ).trim() === '';

      fields.topic.classList.toggle(
        'zt-required-invalid',
        topicMissing
      );
    }


    fields.subtopic.classList.toggle(
      'zt-required-invalid',
      subtopicMissing
    );


    var error =
      document.querySelector(
        '.zt-request-validation-error'
      );

    if (error) {
      error.classList.toggle(
        'is-visible',
        topicMissing || subtopicMissing
      );
    }
  }


  /**
   * Bind fields after node render.
   */
  whenEvent(
    'render:finish',
    function () {

      var fields =
        getRequestFields();

      /*
       * Neither supported form is present.
       */
      if (!fields.subtopic) {
        return;
      }


      ensureValidationMessage();


      /**
       * Bind Topic if this is the standard form.
       */
      if (
        fields.topic &&
        !fields.topic.dataset
          .requiredValidationBound
      ) {

        fields.topic.addEventListener(
          'change',
          function () {

            assignSessionVar(
              'sf_Topic__c',
              fields.topic.value
            );

            refreshValidationState();
          }
        );

        fields.topic.dataset
          .requiredValidationBound =
          'true';
      }


      /**
       * Bind Subtopic for both form types.
       */
      if (
        !fields.subtopic.dataset
          .requiredValidationBound
      ) {

        fields.subtopic.addEventListener(
          'change',
          function () {

            assignSessionVar(
              'sf_Sub_Topic__c',
              fields.subtopic.value
            );

            refreshValidationState();
          }
        );

        fields.subtopic.dataset
          .requiredValidationBound =
          'true';
      }


      /*
       * Don't show errors immediately when the
       * node first loads.
       */
      if (fields.topic) {
        fields.topic.classList.remove(
          'zt-required-invalid'
        );
      }

      fields.subtopic.classList.remove(
        'zt-required-invalid'
      );
    }
  );


  /**
   * ========================================================
   * NAVIGATION GUARD
   * ========================================================
   */
  document.addEventListener(
    'click',
    function (event) {

      var fields =
        getRequestFields();

      /*
       * No supported form on this node.
       */
      if (!fields.subtopic) {
        return;
      }


      /*
       * Allow the user to interact with the form itself.
       */
      if (
        event.target.closest(
          '.zt-form-card'
        )
      ) {
        return;
      }


      /*
       * Only inspect clickable navigation controls.
       */
      var navigationControl =
        event.target.closest(
          'button, a, input[type="button"], input[type="submit"]'
        );

      if (!navigationControl) {
        return;
      }


      /*
       * Valid form: allow navigation.
       */
      if (requestDetailsAreValid()) {
        return;
      }


      /*
       * Invalid form: stop navigation.
       */
      event.preventDefault();
      event.stopPropagation();
      event.stopImmediatePropagation();

      showValidationErrors();

    },
    true
  );

})();
</script>

(function () {
  /**
   * Shows or hides the thumbs-down comments section.
   */
  function setCommentsVisibility($widget, shouldShow) {
    var $comments = $widget.find('.ai-feedback-comments');

    $comments
      .toggleClass('is-visible', shouldShow)
      .attr('aria-hidden', shouldShow ? 'false' : 'true');

    if (shouldShow) {
      window.setTimeout(function () {
        $comments.find('.ai-feedback-comments-input').trigger('focus');
      }, 0);
    }
  }

  whenEvent('render:finish', function () {
    var $widgets = jQuery('.ai-feedback-wrap');

    if (!$widgets.length) return;

    $widgets.each(function () {
      var $widget = jQuery(this);

      if ($widget.data('ai-feedback-bound')) return;
      $widget.data('ai-feedback-bound', true);

      /*
       * Handle thumbs-up and thumbs-down selection.
       */
      $widget.on('click', '.ai-feedback-btn', function () {
        var $btn = jQuery(this);
        var feedbackValue = $btn.attr('data-feedback');
        var $hidden = $widget.find(
          'input[name="ai_feedback"]'
        );
        var $commentsInput = $widget.find(
          'textarea[name="ai_feedback_comments"]'
        );
        var $error = $widget.find(
          '.ai-feedback-comments-error'
        );

        // Highlight the selected thumb.
        $widget
          .find('.ai-feedback-btn')
          .removeClass('selected');

        $btn.addClass('selected');

        // Update the hidden Zingtree form-data field.
        $hidden.val(feedbackValue);

        // Clear any previous validation message.
        $error.text('');

        if (feedbackValue === 'thumbs_down') {
          /*
           * Stay on this screen and allow the user to explain
           * why the generated email was not helpful.
           */
          setCommentsVisibility($widget, true);
        } else {
          /*
           * Hide and clear comments if the user changes their
           * selection from thumbs-down to thumbs-up.
           */
          setCommentsVisibility($widget, false);
          $commentsInput.val('');

          assignSessionVar(
            'ai_feedback_comments',
            ''
          );
        }

        assignSessionVar(
          'ai_feedback',
          feedbackValue
        );
      });

      /*
       * Keep ai_feedback_comments synchronized while typing.
       */
      $widget.on(
        'input',
        '.ai-feedback-comments-input',
        function () {
          var comments = jQuery(this).val();

          assignSessionVar(
            'ai_feedback_comments',
            comments
          );

          $widget
            .find('.ai-feedback-comments-error')
            .text('');
        }
      );

      /*
       * Submit the thumbs-down feedback after comments
       * have been entered.
       */
      $widget.on(
        'click',
        '.ai-feedback-submit',
        function () {
          var comments = String(
            $widget
              .find('.ai-feedback-comments-input')
              .val() || ''
          ).trim();

          var $error = $widget.find(
            '.ai-feedback-comments-error'
          );

          /*
           * Remove this validation block if comments should
           * be optional.
           */
          if (!comments) {
            $error.text(
              'Please enter a comment before submitting.'
            );

            $widget
              .find('.ai-feedback-comments-input')
              .trigger('focus');

            return;
          }

          $error.text('');

          assignSessionVar(
            'ai_feedback',
            'thumbs_down'
          );

          assignSessionVar(
            'ai_feedback_comments',
            comments
          );

          do_button_click(
            8,
            null,
            'AI feedback submitted',
            'thumbs_down'
          );
        }
      );
    });
  });

  whenEvent('formDataUpdated', function (changes) {
    if (!changes || typeof changes !== 'object') return;

    if (
      !Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(
        changes,
        'ai_feedback'
      )
    ) {
      return;
    }

    var feedbackValue = changes.ai_feedback;

     * Thumbs-up can continue immediately.
     *
     * Thumbs-down remains on the current screen so the user
     * can enter ai_feedback_comments. Navigation occurs from

# claude.md - Email Automation - Allstar - INT (org 605565 "Brent Thomas - Sandbox")

## Purpose
The single Zingtree workflow on the shared Salesforce case page layout for Corpay UK (Allstar).
Runs the account checks once, reads the queue stamped on the case, and then runs the FAST Admin or
the Homecharge AI journey inside this same tree. Detects intent with an AI Action, drafts a reply
with a second AI Action, shows the agent a case-review dashboard, and sends the approved reply
through Salesforce emailSimple.

Replaces three trees: Email Automation - Router, Fast Admin - INT (783808640) and Allstar
Homecharge - INT. The Tree nodes and the two duplicated front ends are gone; the queue decision is
now a plain Scoring node (10) in front of the two Detect-intent AI Action nodes. 86 nodes across
three trees became 48 in one.

Agreed with Corpay on the 9 Sept standup: "rather than stacking widgets in the Salesforce page
layout, Zingtree team will create one tree with routing logic to follow the Fast Admin or
Chargepass AI journey. Last queue dev ID in Salesforce will be the identifier."

Use cases: FAST Admin (13 intents, ported 1:1 from GT's "Email Automation - AI Actions INT"
109029630 org 123) and Homecharge Phase 1 - Missing Charges, Tariff Update, Update Charger
Details, Password Reset, Compatible Chargers, Payment Query, Resent Onboarding Email
(Charley Gunning documents, 3 and 15 Sept).

## Architecture (47 nodes + this one)

## Data dictionary

- sentiment and confidence_score look unread to the lint and are not. sentiment is merged into

- queue_source_value - the raw Last_Owner_Queue_Name__c value, printed on screen 11.
- queue_route - "fast_admin" | "homecharge" | "" - the only thing router 10 branches on.

  so the two lanes share these names without colliding.
- ai_exception_reason - the intent AI Action's own account of why a case was not handled
  automatically, written by node 13 (FAST Admin) or node 19 (Homecharge). "" whenever the Action

- hc_salesforce_by_intent - THE Homecharge intent -> Topic / Sub Topic map, declared in node 19

- hc_variant_labels - flat variant key -> label map, declared in node 19, parsed by node 26.
- hc_required_checks (JSON array of check names), hc_blocking_checks (JSON array of

- hc_validation_html - node 19 -> screen 21. GUIDANCE ONLY (detected intents, the AI's
  suggestions, what ticking means). Every input on that screen is a native field.
- hc_requester_options, hc_variant_options - node 19 -> the two native dynamic selects on screen
  21, each an array of {label, value} with the AI's suggestion FIRST. Transforms because a native
  dynamic select is one of the two things a transform is for. hc_variant_options is [] when the
  detected intent has no variant group, and the field is hidden anyway.
- hc_has_variant, hc_ask_sender_validated, hc_ask_pairing_checked, hc_ask_account_unlocked,
  hc_ask_screenshots_attached - "yes"/"no" drivers written by node 19 and read ONLY by the
  config.conditional on the matching field of screen 21. One driver per question; node 19's
  checkDrivers map is where a new check gets wired.
- hc_requester_type, hc_response_variant, hc_sender_validated, hc_pairing_checked,
  hc_screenshots_attached, hc_account_unlocked - screen 21 answers. The four checks are required
  Yes/No selects, so node 22 reads "Yes" or "No" and never an absent value. hc_response_variant
  covers hc_tariff_update and hc_payment_query; its select renders only when hc_has_variant is
  "yes".
- hc_agent_required (bool) - node 22 -> router 23.
- sf_Origin ("Zingtree AI"), hc_template_key, hc_copy_approved - nodes 15 / 24.
- hc_manual_changes_required (bool), hc_manual_changes_reason - node 24. The boolean is router
  31's first test; the reason is printed on the dashboard by node 26.
- sf_Energy_Supplier__c, sf_Data_Provider__c - dashboard inputs on screen 30 (Homecharge lane

  other sf_* field does. The API names are placeholders - OPEN ITEM #4.

- HtmlBody, sf_Subject at node 36 - rewritten in place, escaped for their QUOTED positions in

## Conventions and gotchas
- PREREQUISITE: Last_Owner_Queue_Name__c must be in the SELECT list of Connected Object 1263 and
  its _prod twin. Until it is, node 8 reads undefined and every case lands on screen 11. Test Mode
  mocks the field, so the routing logic is testable first.
- The queue -> journey mapping is declared once, in node 8. Do not restate it anywhere else.
- An AI Action node carries exactly one ai_action_id, so the two journeys need their own Detect and
  Generate nodes. That is the only reason the lanes exist; they converge at screen 30.
- The lanes keep their own dashboard scripts (17 / 26) because the two scripts read different
  actions.* aliases. Do not merge them into one script with a dynamic alias lookup.
- Both lanes write email_intent / sentiment / escalate_reason under the same names. Only one lane
  runs per session, so there is one writer per session and no duplicate storage.
- Every Test Mode scenario key starts with test_, and nothing that starts with test_ is an intent
  key. The prefix is also the journey selector: test_hc_ makes node 47 mock an Allstar_Chargepass
  case, test_fast_admin_ a FAST_Admin one (node 47 tests for test_hc_ and defaults to FAST Admin).
  This keeps the 32 scenario keys clear of the real intent keys they used to shadow - the 7
  Homecharge ones (hc_missing_charges, hc_tariff_update, hc_update_charger_details,
  hc_password_reset, hc_compatible_chargers, hc_payment_query, hc_resent_onboarding_email)
  and the 13 FAST Admin ones (active_card_list, order_a_new_card and the rest). Node 8 then resolves queue_route from
  the mocked queue exactly as it does live, so Test Mode exercises the routing decision too.
- Connected Object 187 owns the send_email_simple_int request body. The tree never builds it.
  The template reads exactly five merge fields and nothing else:
      {
        "inputs": [{
          "emailAddresses": "${actions.sfdc_int__case_email_ai.records[0].SuppliedEmail}",
          "ccAddresses": ${transforms.ccAddresses},
          "emailSubject": "${sf_Subject}",
          "emailBody": "${HtmlBody}
",
          "sendRichBody": true,
          "addThreadingTokenToSubject": true,
          "addThreadingTokenToBody": true,
          "relatedRecordId": "${sf_Id}",
          "logEmailOnSend": true,
          "senderType": "OrgWideEmailAddress",
          "senderAddress": "fast.admin@allstarcard.co.uk"
        }]
      }
  ${transforms.ccAddresses} sits BARE - unquoted - so it has to be valid JSON on its own. It is
  the one value the tree has to stage, and node 36 is the node that stages it. Nothing in the
  tree set it between the three-tree merge and 2026-09-15, which is what the send was failing on.
- Never build the request body in a script and merge it as one variable. Node 36 used to end
  with ZT.setFormData("send_email_payload", JSON.stringify(payload)). The template does not read
  that name, and merging a serialized body produced
  JSON_PARSER_ERROR "Unexpected character ('\' (code 92)): was expecting double-quote to start
  field name at [line:1, column:3]" (org 123, 2026-09-15). The sandbox never caught it because
  the placeholder endpoint never parsed anything.
- OPEN ITEM #9 - the Case update does NOT ride in this request. CO 187's template carries no
  caseId and no caseFields, so Topic__c, Sub_Topic__c, Origin, Energy_Supplier__c and
  Data_Provider__c are collected on the dashboard and then dropped. The caseFieldRegistry that
  used to live in node 36 fed nothing and has been removed. Decide with Corpay UK whether those
  fields get added to CO 187's template or a separate Case update Connected Object, then put the
  registry back wherever that lands. Until then the send works and the Case fields do not update.
- An AI Action node carries its own config, separate from the AI Action it points at:
  config "{\"mode\":\"api\",\"instruction\":\"\"}". mode "api" is the one-shot call that writes to
  actions. and follows the continuation; any other mode renders an interactive panel and
  waits for the agent, whatever output format the Action is set to. Setting the Action to JSON does
  not change it - it is a property of the node, not of the Action.
- Write config as a JSON STRING, not as an object. Zingtree's own export emits the string form; a
  hand-authored file that used a real object is what made nodes open a conversation after import
  (seen 2026-09-14 on the Homecharge tree's nodes 4 and 13). Diff a suspect tree's config against
  a genuine export before assuming the mode itself is wrong.
- Every *_html string a content node renders goes to ZT.setTransformData and is rendered as
  ${transforms.} - NEVER setFormData with a bare ${} merge field. A form-data merge
  field does not reliably render markup: on the Homecharge validation screen (21) the select
  survived but the checkbox inputs were dropped, leaving the three checklist labels as one run
  of text and blocking the agent on a required field (live, org 123, 2026-09-15, case
  500Ad00000cvWYMIA2). Screen 21 no longer renders inputs at all - see the native-fields rule
  below - so that failure mode cannot come back there, but the rule still governs every other
  block this tree renders. The UK source of truth tree 619153300 is the proof: every block it
  renders - case_review_html, requestFormHtml, multipleSubtopicsFormHtml,
  email_sent_summary_html - is a transform, and only HtmlBody, which is a payload value rather
  than a screen, is form data. The three-tree merge moved all seven of this tree's blocks to
  form data; 2026-09-15 moved them back. The seven pairs: 17/26 -> 30, 17/26 -> 33, 17/26 -> 32,
  19 -> 21, 27 -> 28, 39 -> 41, 45 -> 46. Plain scalars printed on a screen
  (queue_source_value, ai_bypass_reason, ai_exception_reason, errorEmailMessage) stay form data.
- HOW EACH CALL IS GRADED, and why the two kinds differ:
    Connected Object - the response code, e.g. send._zt_meta.response.code on node 39, which
    only reads the composite result on a 2xx. In Test Mode node 47 seeds all four SFDC
    responses with _zt_meta: { response: { code: 200 } }, so the same grading runs on mock
    data. A mocked SFDC response without that block breaks node 39 - keep it on every seed.
    AI Action - the output field the script needs (intent.email_intent !== undefined). The AI
    Actions run LIVE in org 605565 for these use cases, mocked SFDC data or not, and on the
    Test Mode run of 2026-09-15 the live intent response carried no _zt_meta - reading
    intent._zt_meta.response.code threw "cannot read undefined 'response'". Grading on the
    output field is correct whether or not the metadata turns up, which is why it is written
    that way; do not swap it back to a _zt_meta read on the strength of one session's data.
  Either way a response that never arrived must not read as "no intent matched" on screen 29 -
  nodes 13 and 19 route that to escalation with ai_exception_reason saying the check returned no
  result. Nothing infers success from the shape of a payload; there are no [].concat(x || [])
  stand-ins for "did this return anything".
- Every *_html string is still collapsed to one line before it is stored - newlines in a merge
  field have rendered as 
 and broken the grid layouts (seen live 2026-09-11).
- Scoring nodes carry advanced_logic_node "1" and mark their else branch with op "def". With
  advanced_logic_node "0" the editor opens the node in Simple mode, shows empty
  Variable / Operator / Value fields and ignores logic_expression entirely.
- Client-side JS in script_code (request-details validation, rich editor sync, AI feedback widget)
  was byte-identical in all three source trees and is carried over unchanged. It calls
  do_button_click(8, ...) for the AI feedback widget - a source-tree button reference that has
  never been verified live, and node numbers moved in this merge. Check it on the dashboard screen.
- The Email node (42) really sends to ZingtreeTeam@allstarcard.co.uk on a failed send. Test Mode
  never reaches it (the mocked send succeeds).
- Only driver Homecharge copy has been signed off. A fleet run is re-framed by the generation
  prompt and flagged on the dashboard through hc_copy_approved. See OPEN ITEM #3.
- Edison and Chargelink have no integration. Screen 21 records the agent's attestation; anything
  unticked routes to the escalation notice rather than drafting a reply.
- SCREEN 21'S INPUTS ARE NATIVE FIELDS, NOT DYNAMIC HTML. The requester and the approved-reply
  selects are native dynamic selects reading transforms.hc_requester_options /
  transforms.hc_variant_options; each Edison / Salesforce check is a required native Yes/No
  select shown by config.conditional on its hc_ask_* driver. This replaced zt-data checkbox
  markup that rendered without its tick boxes on roughly every other case tested, leaving a
  mandatory field unanswerable. Three reasons it stays native: a zt-data input cannot enforce
  required, an unticked checkbox does not read back reliably through getVariableValue, and the
  markup is no longer ours to get dropped. A required conditional field is safe - required only
  bites once the field renders. Dynamic HTML on this screen is display text only.
- Adding a check is three edits, all of them declarative: a row in requiredChecksByIntent (or
  blockingChecksByIntent), a row in checkDrivers, and one native field on screen 21 carrying the
  question text and its conditional. Node 22 never changes - it reads the resolved lists.
- The validation checklist is per intent, not global. requiredChecksByIntent in node 19 decides
  what screen 21 asks for. Compatible Chargers and Resent Onboarding Email take no account-level
  action and their use case documents carry no step 3, so they ask for nothing and the Validation
  block does not render at all. Node 22 reads the resolved list rather than restating the
  conditions - adding an intent never means editing node 22.
- hc_screenshots_attached is a BLOCKING check: ticking it ENDS AI handling instead of clearing
  it. Blocking checks live in blockingChecksByIntent, keyed by check name with the escalation
  reason as the value, so a second one is one row.
- A response variant whose approved template carries a placeholder sets hc_manual_changes_required
  in node 24, and router 31 tests it FIRST - ahead of the multi-intent branch - so the send path
  cannot be reached without an edit. Today that is underpayment_response, whose template leaves
  [INSERT UNIT RATE EXCLUDING VAT] for the driver's kWh rate. Nothing is lost by skipping screen
  32: screen 33 carries the Topic and Sub Topic selects too.
- Bypass gate (node 6) field mapping is OPEN ITEM #1 - confirm with Corpay UK.

  points at. Importing it as a new tree means updating the layout.
